plan.question: Does the existing aligned no-row half-allocation model retain its improvement over native full normalization and the original target-aware reference across prospectively paired seeds 43 and 44, with the empty/short-history tradeoff reported rather than optimized away? The latest matched-parameter seed42 receipts give half/full AUC 0.6151021885074872/0.6149816911798147 and Logloss 0.19653258393542125/0.19656340759133067 on 3,234,051 impressions. Half therefore gains 0.00012049732767249743 AUC but worsens both metrics for empty and 1-16 histories, together 50,077 impressions and 1,754 positives. Earlier aligned replays reproduce these exported metrics without providing independent initializations. The short-history full-gradient fallback loses population AUC, while the historical magnitude maximum fails exact-source score replay and later magnitude contrasts have mixed signs. The crossed-pairing half benefit also prevents treating the half effect as evidence of an aligned-only semantic mechanism. Retrieve evidence needed to distinguish a reproducible optimization effect from seed sensitivity, generic conditioning, shared-parameter coupling and adaptive validation/checkpoint selection. Positive paired-seed effects would support repeatable performance, not semantic mediation; mixed or reversed effects would weaken robustness. Further seed42 implementation sweeps are lower priority than resolving this uncertainty and preserving a complete closed-assessment reserve.
